title: Deep Learning-based RF Fingerprint Authentication with Chaotic Antenna Arrays
abstract: Radio frequency (RF) fingerprinting is a tool for authentication using distinct signal distortions. This paper introduces a deep learning-based method for Physically Unclonable Wireless Systems (PUWS) using Chaotic Antenna Arrays (CAAs), tested with 300 simulated CAAs and 3 CNN architectures under varying channel conditions.
problem_statement: Increasing IoT device vulnerabilities require secure authentication. Traditional RF fingerprinting methods face limitations with large-scale devices and dynamic channel conditions.
methodology: Utilizes deep learning (CNNs) with chaotic antenna arrays (CAAs) for authentication. CAAs introduce randomness in antenna geometry and feed lines to generate unique RF fingerprints.
dataset: Simulation data of 300 CAAs, each with 4 antenna elements, under varying channel conditions and Doppler shifts.
performance: ResNet-50 achieved 99.2% accuracy with CAA fingerprints, surpassing traditional RF fingerprinting's 63% accuracy. CAA-enhanced fingerprints show significant improvement under Rayleigh fading.
contribution: Introduces PUWS with CAAs for hardware-based authentication, demonstrating deep learning's effectiveness in enhancing RF fingerprinting for secure IoT systems.
limitations: Relies on simulation data; real-world environmental factors and hardware constraints may affect performance.
future_work: Explore real-world deployment, additional CNN architectures, and integration with existing security frameworks.

title: A Comprehensive Survey on Feature Extraction Techniques Using I/Q Imbalance in RFFI
abstract: The proliferation of IoT devices has intensified the need for secure authentication. Traditional encryption-based solutions impose high computational overhead on resource-limited IoT nodes. RFFI exploits hardware-induced imperfections like I/Q imbalance as unique identifiers, but challenges remain in standardizing feature extraction methods and maintaining accuracy across environments.
problem_statement: Challenges in standardizing feature extraction methods, maintaining high accuracy across diverse environments, and efficiently handling large-scale IoT deployments.
methodology: Comprehensive review of I/Q imbalance-based RFFI techniques, discussion of other hardware impairments (power amplifier nonlinearity, oscillator imperfections), and analysis of ML/DL approaches for device identification.
dataset: LTE mobile devices, USRP platforms, simulated signals with 5 analog transmitters (400 signals, 50% train/test split).
performance: Adaptive filters achieve 96.01% accuracy; channel-correlation methods show robustness to environmental variations; signal space representation excels in moderate SNR (15 dB) with low memory usage.
contribution: Comprehensive survey of I/Q imbalance-based RFFI techniques, analysis of hardware impairments, and evaluation of ML/DL-driven solutions for device identification.
limitations: Standardization challenges, accuracy in dynamic/hostile environments, scalability to massive IoT networks.
future_work: Efficient methods for resource-constrained systems, dynamic/multipath environments, and hybrid approaches balancing transient/steady-state features.
